headline: Wrap: Wall Street turned an AI rout into a rotation by the close, while a Houthi strike claim on Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery lifted oil

findings.headline: The rebound was a rotation, not an all-clear
findings.body: The Dow wiped out an intraday drop of more than 1,100 points to close higher, with small caps, materials, financials and industrials leading while tech and chips lagged. Nvidia still closed down 3.9% after losing about 8% early, so the AI financing worry was trimmed, not resolved. Europe shut before the US turn, which is why its banks and tech carry the full damage into tomorrow's open.

findings.headline: Oil puts back a Gulf risk premium ahead of the 29 November OPEC+ meeting
findings.body: Yemen's Houthis said they attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, the kingdom's largest and part of a major crude export complex, giving Brent its highest settle since 13 November. The EIA crude build of 1.1 million barrels was smaller than the 1.5 million expected, and pre-holiday short covering added to the move. The bigger test is the 29 November OPEC+ meeting, with the UAE outside quota limits and Iraq pushing for more capacity, so 2027 supply policy is still open.

findings.headline: Priced for tomorrow: a December hike, and thin holiday trading
findings.body: After the hot core PCE and the upward GDP revision, markets treat a quarter-point Fed hike on 8-9 December as close to certain, so the open question has moved to 2027. US markets are shut for Thanksgiving on Thursday and close early on Friday, leaving Asia and Europe to trade the US recovery on thin liquidity. Korean and Taiwanese chipmakers took the hardest hits overnight and are the first test of whether the late US bounce carries over.

sources.label: Yahoo Finance: PCE inflation heats up, solidifying a Fed rate hike in December

view: Our view: Buying the dip in cyclicals while still selling the AI leaders says investors are repositioning, not giving up, but with volatility still high and a hike locked in, a holiday-thin session can swing hard either way. Oil is the one market adding risk premium rather than shedding it, and OPEC+ on Sunday decides whether that sticks.
